display.title: Tanya Chapter 32: Ahavas Yisroel, the Heart of the Tanya
display.summary_short: A Yiddish Tanya shiur on chapter 32, the 'heart' of the Tanya: loving every Jew simply because he is a Jew, and why this mitzvah is the whole Torah.
display.summary_long: Rabbi Yosef Goldstein's Yiddish shiur on Tanya chapter 32, called the heart of the Tanya. The Frierdiker Rebbe stressed love for every single Jew, a love that depends on no reason. In a story, great tzaddikim each named the special quality of a Jew, and the Baal Shem Tov answered that a Jew's greatest quality is simply that he is a Jew. The chapter teaches that one who treats the body as secondary and the soul as primary can truly love another Jew, since all souls come from one Father and are truly brothers. Hillel called 'love your fellow as yourself' the whole Torah, illustrated by the body whose limbs all depend on one another, and by Moshe Rabbeinu and the Jewish people as head and feet. The Shechinah rests only where Jews are united: 'bless us, our Father, all of us as one'. A chain of bar mitzvah questions among the Chabad Rebbeim explains why one accepts this mitzvah before davening. The Rebbe's teaching about Shemini Atzeres, 'your parting is hard for Me', shows Hashem's pain at division among Jews, and the class ends with how to love a Jew who sins: hate the deed, but love the person.
display.lesson: Love every Jew simply because he is a Jew; this love is the foundation of the whole Torah and brings Hashem's greatest delight.

segments.title: Chapter 32: the heart of the Tanya
segments.summary: Like the heart in the body, this chapter is the life-center of the book.

segments.title: Loving every single Jew
segments.summary: The Frierdiker Rebbe's emphasis on love for every Jew, a love that depends on no reason.

segments.title: The Baal Shem Tov: what is special about a Jew?
segments.summary: At a gathering of tzaddikim, the Baal Shem Tov answered that a Jew's greatest quality is that he is a Jew.

segments.title: Body secondary, soul primary: all Jews are brothers
segments.summary: All souls come from one Father, so Jews are truly brothers; only the body divides them.

segments.title: The whole Torah on one foot, and the mashal of one body
segments.summary: Hillel's answer, the limbs of one body, and Moshe Rabbeinu and the people as head and feet.

segments.title: The Shechinah rests where Jews are one
segments.summary: The root of the Torah is raising the soul above the body, and 'bless us, our Father, all as one'.

segments.title: The bar mitzvah question: why accept Ahavas Yisroel before davening
segments.summary: Each Chabad Rebbe let his son ask a question at bar mitzvah; the Rebbe Rashab explained this custom of the Siddur.

segments.title: 'Your parting is hard for Me'
segments.summary: The Rebbe's explanation of Hashem's words on Shemini Atzeres and His pain at division among Jews.

segments.title: Loving Hashem through loving His children
segments.summary: One cannot love Hashem while hating a Jew, who is a part of Hashem.

segments.title: Hillel's 'guest', and loving a Jew who sins
segments.summary: Hate the deed but love the person, and keep trying to draw him close.
